recipes.name: Lemon Basmati Rice
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat; add rice, ginger, and lemon zest and cook about 1 minute. Add lemon juice and chicken broth; bring to a boil. Cover the pot; simmer until liquid absorbed and rice tender, 18 to 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Basmati Rice
raw_recipe.description: This delicious and easy side dish goes great with fish!

review.reviewBody: This is the best rice recipe I have ever tasted! I made it exactly as stated in the recipe and I wouldn't change a thing!

I made this in the Instant Pot. As such, I modified slightly, I soaked the rice. I used butter instead of canola oil, and sauted the lemon zest and ginger before adding the soaked rice. I then added 1 and 1/4 cups chicken broth, lemon juice and salt and pepper. I used Manual High setting for 4 minutes and then Natural Release for 10 minutes. It turned out great!

I followed the recipe to the letter the first time I made it and immediately I noticed a flaw. Too much liquid. The rice came out sticky. I checked my bag of basmati rice and the recipe on the bag stated 1 1/2 cups liquid to 1 cup of rice. This is what I use when I cook basmati rice. I recommend adding the 1 1/2 tablespoons on fresh lemon juice the adding enough chicken broth to make 11/2 cups of liquid. Problem of mushy, sticky rice solved.

This was awesome. I made it in my rice cooker using Forbidden Rice, which has a nutty flavor and striking black color. I used ground ginger as I didn't have fresh, and substituted grapeseed oil for the canola. My lemon was quite large, so I used about 1-1/2 T of the zest, and 1/3 cup juice. Served with sauteed mahi mahi. Will definitely make this again.

Tried it & loved it! 1 full lemon to 1 cup of rice would have been too tart for my taste, so I increased the amount of rice to 2 cups & doubled the amount of water. I also decreased fresh lemon juice to 3/4 of a lemon. Once steamed, the rice was the perfect vehicle for Asian spicy tofu paired with balsamic green beans. Absolutely delicious!

I make this every time I make curry or tikka masala...it is perfect...note, i always use ground ginger and it is fine...if you are pressed for time, use minute rice, it is still delicious...a little cilantro is also great in it...when making this, i always put the broth and seasonings, lemon juice, etc in a pot and taste it before adding the rice...that way the flavors balance...if using basmati, i par cook it,,then add it to the rest of the ingredients...when using minute rice, i just throw it in...it is great with seafood, indian food, mexican food (add cilantro, omit ginger and add a little mexican seasoning)...cant go wrong

Very good side for any dish, vegetable or meat. However, if I may suggest; add an equal amount of butter to the canola oil, add Kosher salt and WHITE pepper to the broth and reduce heat to low after a hard boil is achieved. 
Almost good on its own!

This was really good! I used lemon juice and added a clove of minced garlic, and a couple dashes of no-salt seasoning. I also cooked the salt and pepper in. We all liked it, and will probably make it again.

Brilliant recipe. I made it for the first time today and only used half a lemon and half a lemon zest. To give it abit more vibrant colour I added abit of Tumeric. I can't get enough of the flavorful rice. Can't wait for supper time

The family accepted the dish without issue in conjunction with Baked Salmon with Mustard-Dill sauce. The lemon complimented the Salmon graciously. 

I made this recipe in the rice cooker adding rice, lemon, ginger to chicken broth instead of water. I used both juice and zest of fresh lemon (recipe is a bit ambiguous on this point) and must have got too much pulp from squeezed juice in the mix as the rice was a bit sticky. I cooked a little longer to reduce the water content and firm up the rice. Worked like a charm.

I make this often especially with fish & chicken.
It's PERFECT! Can also be made in a rice cooker,
so easy!
Loved this rice and I paired it with Lemon Butter Chicken. I didn't have ginger root and not sure if I even want it in the rice. It's definitely a recipe I will make many more time .....
This was amazing, exactly as is, served with shrimp scampi and broccoli. Will be a repeat.

The lemon juice is the star which was exactly what I was looking for today. The ginger flavor was pretty much lost, but I did use ginger paste in the tube, not ginger root. I had a few almond slices left in a bag, so I added them to the rice. Cooked up beautifully, plenty moist, and I’d make this again.
Excellent! Served with Restaurant Style Pork Chops and Apple Rings (NYTimes), broccoli, Irish Bannock for Luck in 2021 on New Year's Day.
This was good but didn’t fine it had much a lemony taste to it. Maybe my lemon wasn’t big enough?? I’ll definitely try making it again.
I was searching for a Lemon Scented Basmati Rice dish my local Central Market H-E-B prepares as a deli item and this was the closest base recipe I could find to modify
Delicious.. next time I will lighten the lemon. It's a little strong . Still delicious but will definitely reduce the lemon.. just a little over half of what it calls for.
